key_insight: This paper asks whether diffusion-based LLMs are less transparent because they do more computation in a continuous latent space. The key idea is to break transparency into "variable transparency" and "algorithmic transparency" so we can separately measure whether the model’s intermediate states and overall reasoning process are understandable.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of evaluating reasoning transparency in DiffusionGemma, where standard notions of interpretability may not apply cleanly because much of the computation happens in continuous latent states rather than discrete token-by-token steps.
method: Decompose transparency into two parts: variable transparency (understanding intermediate states) and algorithmic transparency (understanding the reasoning procedure).
Analyze DiffusionGemma’s intermediate snapshots to see whether its hidden computational states can be interpreted meaningfully.
Compare transparency properties of diffusion-style computation with more conventional LLM reasoning behavior.
impact: This helps researchers and practitioners understand whether diffusion-based language models can still be debugged, audited, and trusted despite their less discrete internal computation. It also provides a clearer framework for measuring interpretability in future non-standard generative architectures.
